source.locator: lines 20-23, proof of first incompleteness statement

findings.finding: The proof changes the theorem's computable axiomatizability hypothesis to mere axiomatization before claiming decidability.
findings.controlling_evidence: The theorem assumes axiomatizability, and the immediately preceding lemma proves decidability from completeness plus a computable set of axioms. Mere axiomatization does not imply decidability.
findings.required_translation_handling: Retain the source token identity, render the intended computable-axiomatizability sense, and add an adjacent OLTETCP-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The final reduction uses the malformed expression #(!D_S(numeral u)) as the code in R's first argument.
findings.controlling_evidence: R was defined to take the code of a one-free-variable formula D(u), and the identical construction in the preceding consistent-extension proof uses Gn{!D_S(u)}.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use Gn{!D_S(u)} and add an adjacent OLTETCP-002 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 20-25 and 36-38, interpretability theorem and first ZFC corollary

findings.finding: The theorem excludes decidable consistent extensions, but the corollary drops consistency and therefore also purports to exclude inconsistent extensions.
findings.controlling_evidence: The theorem explicitly requires a consistent extension. An inconsistent extension proves every sentence and is decidable, so the unqualified corollary is false.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore the consistency qualification in the ZFC corollary and add an adjacent OLTETCP-003 disclosure.
